discovery: Invention of the high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) based on modulation-doped semiconductor heterojunctions
motivation: In 1979-1980 Takashi Mimura conceived and demonstrated the high-electron-mobility transistor, placing a two-dimensional electron gas at a modulation-doped heterointerface under gate control. Separating the electrons from their ionized donors removed impurity scattering and gave very high mobility and speed. This insight in device physics, grounded in careful heterostructure crystal growth, became the basis of the low-noise amplifiers in satellite receivers, radio telescopes, mobile phones and wireless base stations. The same two-dimensional electron gas concept, carried over to AlGaN/GaN heterostructures, is now the leading GaN transistor for energy-efficient power conversion and high-frequency electronics, cutting electricity losses worldwide. The HEMT is a clear example of physics understood at a crystal interface turning into technology that serves all of humanity and saves energy. I nominate Dr. Mimura for this invention.
